realization.note: Regenerated defect projections against the CURRENT Defect Data.xlsx (fixes: (1) length-tie ties among candidates now broken randomly instead of favoring the first-listed/highest-defect row in a tied-length block; (2) pool now guaranteed consistent with this run's spreadsheet, resolving a prior mismatch where the spreadsheet had been edited after the stems were originally generated. Stem/segment geometry (heights, lengths, BU position, diameter class) reused verbatim from the prior realization -- only the mill-log matching and defect placement were redone.

schemaNote: Each stem carries 'plot' and 'treeNum' tracing back to source data. Forked trees use decimal sub-IDs (e.g. '2-3.1', '2-3.2') for each fork in cut order, per real skidding/bucking practice. Stems flagged complexityTag='complex' involve forks and should be reviewed. FORK-SPLITTING FIX (2026-09-13): the terminating stem's profile now correctly ends at the last log BEFORE a fork marker, not at the fork-base row itself, eliminating false 'backwards taper' artifacts previously seen in 68 stems. MINIMUM STEM LENGTH EXCLUSION -- RAISED TO 10.5ft (2026-09-13): any fork-derived stem shorter than 10.5ft is EXCLUDED, since it cannot be bucked into any usable product (10.5ft reflects a realistic minimum sawlog length with trim allowance below the common 12ft product length). This threshold was raised from an initial 8.0ft floor after review. 6 stems total are now excluded for this reason: 4-1.1 (6.0ft), 7-1.3 (7.0ft), 7-6.1 (6.0ft), 8-15.2 (8.7ft), 8-15.3 (8.2ft), 9-9.1 (5.4ft) -- all short slivers of wood between closely-spaced fork points. Logged in excludedTrees with a 'too short to be a usable bucking stem' reason, never silently dropped. Total stem count is now 339 (down from 345 pre-fix, 341 at the earlier 8.0ft floor). TAPER ANOMALY FLAGGING: every stem's meta.taperAnomalies lists any local diameter INCREASE along its profile (negative taper). Only entries with flaggedAsLikelyError=true (increase >= 2.0in) indicate probable data errors warranting review. Shape defects (sweep, crook) modeled geometrically in meta.shapeDefects. Quality defects (section/sector/interior) in meta.qualityDefects as metadata only. Mill-study surface defects (meta.millDefectProjections) are POINT DEFECTS WITH PHYSICAL FOOTPRINT: each defect drawn from a matched real mill log (species+diameter+B/U, falling back to diameter+B/U if <15 matching logs; length-proximity bootstrap from 5 closest-length candidates) is assigned a random position and a footprint length sampled from its size class: le3in -> uniform(0.5,3.0)in, 3to6in -> uniform(3.0,6.0)in, gt6in -> uniform(6.0,12.0)in (EXPLICIT ASSUMPTION). Defects placed per side (1-4) with random side rotation. Within each side only, overlapping/touching footprints merge into a mergedZone; different sides never merge. Schema is a FIXED CONTRACT: each projection has segStartHeightFt, segEndHeightFt, segmentLengthFt, sides.side1-side4, each with defectCounts (le3in/3to6in/gt6in), individualDefects, and mergedZones (zoneStartIn, zoneEndIn, zoneLengthIn, memberDefectCount). SPECIES CODES: CH=Cherry, HM=Hard Maple, SM=Soft Maple, CO=Chestnut Oak, HK=Hickory, RO=Red Oak, WO=White Oak, YP=Yellow Poplar, WAL=Walnut are CONFIRMED. BO, SO, AB, SW, RM, SG, SY, DLM, SPS remain UNCONFIRMED and always fall back to diameter+B/U matching. *** THIS IS ONE REALIZATION *** -- no fixed seed; re-running produces DIFFERENT defect placements on the same corrected geometry. Every defect carries sourceMillLogRowId for traceability. See Stem_Reconstruction_Methodology.md and Mill_Defect_Projection_Methodology.md.
